reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
Friday used to mean something specific. It meant the countdown clock in my head starting around 3pm, the tension of waiting, the ritual of the first drink. For years I thought getting sober would mean Fridays became grief days — the day I most missed the person I used to be.

What actually happened is stranger and quieter. Fridays became Fridays again. A drive home where I actually notice the light on the trees changing. A dinner I taste. A conversation with someone I love where I'm actually there for the words, not planning my next move toward the bar. The remarkable thing about a sober Friday isn't fireworks — it's the return of ordinary evening. The ability to end a week and just be in it.

Durant's line about habit gets quoted so much it's almost worn smooth, but read it again. We are what we repeatedly do. Not what we intend, not what we promise ourselves on January 1st. What we do on a Tuesday afternoon and a Friday night when nobody's watching. Sobriety isn't a single dramatic decision — it's a stack of small ordinary ones. Showing up. Making the call. Going to bed clear-headed. Waking up tomorrow as someone you recognize. That stack is the whole life.
reflection.meditation: What ordinary thing has sobriety given back to me that I once thought I'd lose?

affirmations: I am building a life from the small choices I make when no one is watching.
Today I can be fully present for the people in front of me.
I trust that an ordinary sober evening is worth more than any night I traded it for.

gratitude.prayer: I'm grateful for a Friday I don't have to survive. Grateful for the version of me that made the hard call years ago so this version could sit here clear-headed, tired in the honest way, tasting the end of a real week. Grateful for the people who stayed, and the ones who showed me how to do this before I believed I could.
gratitude.closing: One more day, received and returned with thanks.
